Explain how a siphon transfers water between two containers, why the outlet must be lower than the source surface, and how air entering the tube can interrupt flow. Use plain accurate prose. Aim for approximately 120–170 English tokens.

message.content:
A siphon is a continuous, water-filled tube that carries water from one container to another. To start it, the tube must be filled so there is no air gap. Once flowing, gravity pulls the water down the longer, lower outlet side. That falling water creates a lower pressure in the top part of the tube, so atmospheric pressure on the source container helps push more water up and over the bend.

The outlet must be lower than the water surface in the source container because the downward pull on the outlet side must be greater than the lift needed on the source side. If the outlet is not lower, there is no net driving force to keep water moving.

If air enters the tube, it can break the continuous column of water. Then pressure is no longer transmitted through the whole tube, and the siphon slows or stops.
